When a document becomes active for the first time after it is opened, FreeCAD examines all Jobs of the document and shows the dialog only when a minimum of one tool is different from the library. The check occurs one time for each load of a document, after restore and recompute are complete.

The check at document load occurs only when the preference 'Check for tool updates from the library when opening a document' is set. The Job context-menu entry operates always, with the preference set or not set.

The Assets page of the CAM preferences has the checkbox 'Check for tool updates from the library when opening a document'. The parameter is the boolean `ToolUpdateOnLoad` in `BaseApp/Preferences/Mod/CAM/Tools`. The default is True (set). The checkbox is below the Machines group and is not in a group box.

The dialog title is 'Tool Updates Available'. The text at the top is: "'{}' has tools that differ from the library (newer presets, changed dimensions - e.g. a regrind - or both). The name in the text is the document label at document load and the Job label from the context menu.
The dialog has one row for each Tool Controller whose embedded Tool Bit is stale, not one row for each Tool Bit. A Tool Bit object that two Tool Controllers use gets two rows.

The next free number of a Job is the highest Tool Number of the Tool Controllers in the Job plus 1. It is 1 when the Job has no Tool Controller. A lower number that is not used is not selected.
When the library tool number is free in the Job, or the same tool already uses it, FreeCAD gives that number to the new Tool Controller and does not ask.

When the document has no Job, 'Add to Job' shows a message with the title 'No Job Found' and the text 'Create a Job first.' When the document has more than one Job and no Job was given to the dialog, FreeCAD asks which Job gets the Tool Controllers.

Two Tool Controllers have a tool number conflict only when they have the same `ToolNumber` and their Tool Bits have different `ToolBitID` values. Tool Controllers whose Tool Bits have the same `ToolBitID` can have the same Tool Number; this is how one tool gets more than one set of feeds and speeds.

When the reader changes the tool number in the Tool Controller editor to a number that a different tool in the Job uses, FreeCAD does not change `ToolNumber`, sets the field back to the old number and shows a warning with the title 'Tool Number In Use' and the text 'Tool number {} is already used by {}.' (the number and the label of the Tool Controller that has it).

The command CAM_ToolController ('Tool Controller', tooltip 'Adds a new tool controller to the active job') is not in a menu or a toolbar. It stays registered for macros and opens the Toolbit Selector for the selected Job with the request for a tool number.
An update from the library sets the `Tool` property of the Tool Controller to the new library copy. The update code changes no other property of the Tool Controller.
The GUI page of the CAM preferences (window title 'GUI') has the group box 'Tool Bit Shape Drawing' with four controls. All four parameters are in `BaseApp/Preferences/Mod/CAM`.
'Dimension color (light theme)': color button, parameter `ToolBitDimensionColorLight`, default #111111 (RGB 17, 17, 17), tooltip 'Color of the dimension lines and labels on a light theme'.
'Dimension color (dark theme)': color button, parameter `ToolBitDimensionColorDark`, default #23818d (RGB 35, 129, 141), tooltip 'Color of the dimension lines and labels on a dark theme'.
'Dimension highlight color': color button, parameter `ToolBitDimensionHighlightColor`, default #ff8c00 (RGB 255, 140, 0), tooltip 'Color of the dimension the mouse is pointing at'.

'Tool artwork brightness (dark theme)': spin box with the suffix ' %', parameter `ToolBitArtworkBrightness` (integer), default 85, minimum 10, maximum 100. The tooltip is 'How brightly the tool itself is drawn on a dark theme. The artwork is drawn for a white page, so it is dimmed to keep it from glaring.' The code also limits a stored value to the range 10 to 100.
For the Chamfer Tool Shape, FreeCAD calculates `Diameter` as TipDiameter + 2 × CuttingEdgeHeight × tan(CuttingEdgeAngle / 2). `Diameter` is not an input.

The ToolBit editor does not show a calculated parameter, thus the Chamfer editor form has no `Diameter` field. The property view shows the Chamfer `Diameter` as read-only. FreeCAD calculates the value again when the Tool Bit properties are updated.

The Chamfer Tool Shape has these parameters and labels: `CuttingEdgeAngle` 'Cutting edge angle', `CuttingEdgeHeight` 'Cutting edge height', `Diameter` 'Diameter', `Flutes` 'Flutes', `Length` 'Overall tool length', `ShankDiameter` 'Shank diameter', `TipDiameter` 'Tip diameter'. Only the Chamfer shape was changed to have a calculated parameter in this unit.

The preset dialog (window title 'Edit preset') has the group box 'Notes' with a text field for more than one line. The text is saved in the key "notes" of the preset record. Empty notes are saved as null.
The table of the Presets tab has the columns 'Name', 'Material', 'Op type', 'Surface speed', 'Chipload' and 'Notes'. The 'Notes' cell shows the notes on one line and the tooltip shows the full text.
The buttons of the Presets tab are 'Add preset', 'Edit', 'Copy' and 'Delete', in this sequence. A double-click on a table row opens the preset for edit.

A preset must have a name. When the 'Name:' field is empty or has only spaces, OK shows a warning with the title 'Name required' and the text 'Give the preset a name.' and the dialog stays open. The placeholder text of the field is "e.g. 'Aluminum aggressive'".

The identity of a preset is the name together with the material and the op type. Two presets of one Tool Bit can have the same name only if the material or the op type is different. If all three are the same, OK shows a warning with the title 'Duplicate preset' and the text "This tool already has a preset named '%s' for this material and op type." and the dialog stays open.

'Copy' operates only when a preset is selected. It opens the preset dialog with the values of the selected preset and with the name selected for edit. On OK, FreeCAD adds a new preset; the selected preset does not change. The name rule also applies, thus the reader must change the name, the material or the op type.

The Camotics export writes, for each tool, the keys "units", "shape", "length", "diameter" and "description". "units" is "imperial" when the active unit schema shows the tool diameter in an imperial unit (in, ", thou, ft, '), and "metric" in all other conditions.

The Camotics export writes "diameter" and "length" as numbers in inches when "units" is "imperial" and in millimeters when "units" is "metric". The unit of the diameter decides the unit for the two values of a tool. The `Units` property of the Tool Bit is not used.

The Camotics export rounds "diameter" and "length" to the number of decimals of the Units Decimals preference (integer parameter `Decimals` in `BaseApp/Preferences/Units`; the code uses 2 when the parameter is not set).

The Camotics import reads the "units" key of each tool: "imperial" gives `Diameter` and `Length` in inches, "metric" gives millimeters. When the key is absent or has a different value, the import uses millimeters.

The Camotics shape names are: ballend and taperedballnose to "Ballnose", endmill to "Cylindrical", v-bit and vbit to "Conical", chamfer to "Snubnose". All other Tool Shapes are exported as "Cylindrical". The serializer label is 'Camotics Tool Library' and the file extension is .json.

The file CAM_UpdateDocumentTools.svg is in src/Mod/CAM/Gui/Resources/icons/ and is registered in Path.qrc. It is the icon of the 'Update Tools from Library' context-menu entry and of the 'Tool Updates Available' dialog (window icon and 64 × 64 image at the top).

Read these before the pages are written.

1. Tool number request: the verdict for 32211 says that the dock is made with askToolNumber=True. This is true for the 'Add Toolbit…' command (library/ui/cmd.py:63), for CAM_ToolController (Gui/Controller.py:191) and for the Tool Controller drop-down of an Operation (Op/Gui/Base.py:578). The Job editor Tools tab makes the dock as ToolBitLibraryDock(self.obj), with askToolNumber=False (Main/Gui/Job.py:1330). The 'All Tools' entry is in all three places (show_all_tools=True is fixed in dock.py).

2. Next free number: the default is the highest Tool Number in the Job plus 1 (F36), not the lowest number that is not used.

3. Preset name rule: the plan says 'necessary and unique preset name'. The source makes the name necessary, but unique only together with the material and the op type (F55). Write it this way.

4. Tool number rule: 'different tool' means a different `ToolBitID` (F39). Two embedded copies of the same library Tool Bit are the same tool.

5. Update from the library: the match is in the local library store only, by `ToolBitID` only (F12). The Changes tree is present only when there are geometry changes; a row with only preset changes shows the plain text 'Presets' (F10). The Job context-menu entry operates when the preference is off (F4).

6. Units: the editor fields get the tool precision through the active unit schema, which the ToolBit editor sets to the `Units` of the Tool Bit while it is open (F24, F25). The Camotics export does not use the `Units` property of the Tool Bit; it uses the active unit schema and the Units Decimals preference (F57 to F59). This is the difference that goal 4 needs: Tool Bit files do not follow the two preferences, the Camotics export does.
